claims.interpretation: Development diagnostic of literal extraction over AI-authored fixtures; not evidence of held-out generalization, recommendation quality or rules correctness.

label_authorship.author: AI-authored (Claude Opus 5.5) for W02 development diagnostics
label_authorship.statement: Synthetic, renamed cards and rule text written by the implementing AI. Not independent, not expert-reviewed, not held out; gold values are the author's reading of the supplied text and may be wrong.

claims.scoring_change_not_compiler_change: v2 adds the output_events dimension, scores every emitted dimension or reports it unjudged, adds output_events gold to all labels and revises 8 label values (see the cases file label_revisions). The compiler and search are unchanged, so every v1->v2 difference is a scoring/label change, not a compiler change.

limitations: Gold values were written by the same AI that read the compiler grammar and use its token vocabulary; precision is optimistic and not independent.
Synthetic renamed cards; no real Oracle corpus sample, so coverage is per fixture, not per deck population.
Dimensions the compiler never represents (e.g. death multiplicity, sacrifice fuel) count as unknown, not FP; restrictions and output_events treat an interpreted fact as a complete claim.

output_events scores structured event rows only. Effects the compiler keeps solely as condition prose (pump, gain flying, explore reveal and +1/+1 counter) score wrong because search cannot join on them; they are listed under summary.unjudged.conditions_on_interpreted_labels, so 'wrong' here means 'not emitted as an event', not 'lost entirely'.

Fact fields no dimension reads (input actor/recipient/source_types, output condition/optional, required_rules) are disclosed per label as unjudged_fact_fields, not scored; required_rules is judged only through search dependency gaps.
Search scoring checks labelled source-pair links only; unlabelled links are counted, not judged.
Hashes and exact tokens establish binding, not entailment or rules correctness.

scoring.all_scored_dimensions_correct: partial verdict: every scored dimension is tp and none is unjudged; unread fact fields and condition prose (unread_fact_content) are not judged, so this is not full clause semantic correctness
scoring.coverage: tp/gold; abstentions and unrepresented clauses stay in the denominator
scoring.finite_fuel: only true is labelled; compiler emits true or does not represent it
scoring.fp: interpreted fact value differs from gold (also counted fn)
scoring.output_events: sorted '<event>:<subject>' of output rows; missing, extra or renamed events score wrong
scoring.restrictions: interpreted facts claim full scope, so they assert no restrictions
scoring.tp: interpreted fact value equals gold token set
scoring.unjudged: an emitted dimension with null or absent gold is reported, never tp/fp, and blocks all_scored_dimensions_correct
scoring.unknown: compiler abstained or does not represent the dimension; never tp/fp

scoring_history.blindspot: Alternate-provider review R1 replaced both compiled explore outputs with an invented event; every v1 total, dimension, mechanism score and clause verdict was unchanged. v1 had no output-event dimension and only iterated supplied gold keys.
scoring_history.field_correction: Raw v1 'fully_correct' is kept verbatim as a historical claim. It meant only that every supplied gold key matched; it never judged unread fact fields, so it overstated scope. v2 renames the verdict all_scored_dimensions_correct and does not claim full clause semantic correctness.
